# PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Kolding)

PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Kolding) is a Danish community psychiatric unit whose performance appears in the ADHD-databasen 2024 report, a national quality database tracking treatment pathways for ADHD patients. The unit is cited as a notable underperformer on Indikator 10, a newly introduced quality measure assessing whether adult patients' social support needs were evaluated within 120 days of starting treatment. PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Kolding) achieved only 9% fulfilment of this indicator, based on 3 out of 35 eligible treatment pathways meeting the standard, placing it among the lowest-performing units nationally against a target of 90% [^src1].

This result sits within a broader national picture: Indikator 10 was reported for the first time in the 2024 database, and both the national average (37%) and the regional range (14–52%) fell far short of the 90% quality target. The steering group behind the database discussed possible causes for the shortfall, including registration practices and data quality issues linked to child and adolescent psychiatric outpatient clinics and private hospitals, and resolved to work on improving registration practices going forward [^src1].

Notably, the same unit performed very differently on a separate measure appearing later in the report. On what the data lists as a related indicator (page 56, within the section covering Indikator 11 — which measures whether adult patients are on ADHD medication within 120 days of starting a treatment package), PSY Lokalpsykiatri (Kolding) achieved 77% (60–90) fulfilment, based on 27 out of 35 pathways [^src2]. Indikator 11 was itself newly measured for adults in 2024, following the database's expansion that year to include adult ADHD patients, and showed wide regional variation nationally (from 85% in Region Nordjylland to 37% in Region Hovedstaden), attributed largely to differences in registration practice rather than actual clinical differences [^src2]. Together, these two figures show a unit performing very poorly on the social-support-assessment measure while performing comparatively well on the medication-timeliness measure.
